overview.title: Overview
overview.lead: The Frank AI Interviewer is an automated research agent that conducts real, in-depth customer conversations via voice call — without requiring you to be in the room. It listens, asks intelligent follow-up questions, probes for the "why" behind answers, and delivers structured insights the moment an interview ends.

items: **Who it's for:** Founders, product managers, and marketers who need fast, reliable customer insight without the time and cost of traditional research.

**Why it matters:** Traditional user interviews are slow, expensive ($500–$1,000 per session), and hard to scale. The AI Interviewer makes it possible to run hundreds of interviews in parallel, in 30+ languages, at a fraction of the cost.

**How it's different from surveys:** Surveys are static — they can't follow up, push back, or uncover emotion. The AI Interviewer is dynamic. It adapts in real time, clarifies vague answers, and captures the emotional reasoning behind customer behavior.

items.x: Chat with the AI Analytics assistant. Voice clips (Reals) are created automatically from key moments once an interview completes. Share the interview link with your audience to start generating insights.

items: **Interview format:** Voice call — customers respond through comfortable audio conversation.
**Adaptive questioning:** The AI follows the conversation naturally, probing deeper based on what the customer says, not a rigid script.
**Guided setup in 10 minutes:** A Research AI Agent helps you craft the right interview outline based on your goals.
**Thematic Analysis:** Automatically groups responses into themes with sentiment scores and frequency stats across all interviews.
**AI Analytics Chat:** Ask questions about your data, generate charts, and explore patterns without writing a single line of code.
**Transcripts & highlights:** Replay interviews, read full transcripts, and save the quotes that resonate.
**30+ languages:** Run interviews with customers worldwide; translations are available automatically.
**Parallel scaling:** Run dozens or hundreds of interviews simultaneously with no scheduling bottleneck.
**SOC 2 & GDPR compliant:** Enterprise-grade security and privacy built in.

Step 2. Choose your interview type
Pick the interview type that aligns with what you want to learn from your audience. Three options are presented side by side:
**Discovery & Validation Interviews**
**When to use:** Early-stage research, before building or launching
**Interview types:**

items: Exploratory / Discovery: understand customer needs and pain points
Concept Testing: validate ideas before building
Messaging & Positioning: test how to communicate your value
Pricing & Value Perception: understand willingness to pay

blocks.x: **Goal:** Understand customer needs, test concepts, and validate product-market fit before investing heavily.
**Product Experience Interviews**
**When to use:** During or after development
**Interview types:**

items: **Prototype / Usability Testing:** find friction points in your product
**Pre-Launch "Expectation":** gauge what users expect before release
**Post-Release Satisfaction:** measure how well the product delivered

blocks.x: **Goal:** Spot friction, refine the user experience, and ensure the product delivers on expectations.
**Retention & Growth Interviews**
**When to use:** After launch, optimizing for long-term success
**Interview types:**

items: **Engagement & Habit:** understand what drives regular usage
**Churn / Exit:** learn why customers leave
**Retention & Expansion:** discover upsell and cross-sell opportunities

blocks.x: **Goal:** Uncover drivers of long-term retention, prevent churn, and discover upsell/cross-sell opportunities.

items.title: Match the interview type to your goal.
items.x: Use Discovery Interviews for early-stage research, Churn Interviews inside cancellation flows, and Post-Release Feedback after major feature launches.

items.title: Keep your interview outline focused.
items.x: 4–6 core topics produce better conversations than exhaustive question lists. The AI will probe deeper on its own.

items.title: Share the link in context.
items.x: A link placed at the point of action (e.g., after a user cancels, right after onboarding, or in a tooltip near a feature) gets higher completion rates than cold email blasts.

items.title: Run at least 20 interviews before drawing conclusions.
items.x: Thematic patterns become statistically meaningful at volume. Aim for 20–50 for early signal; 100+ for confident decisions.

items.title: Review sentiment alongside themes.
items.x: A theme that appears frequently but carries negative sentiment is a friction point. A theme with high positive sentiment is a strength to double down on.

items.title: Iterate your outline.
items.x: After your first batch of interviews, review the themes and refine your questions to go deeper on what emerged.

blocks.x: What to look for

items: **High-frequency themes:** Topics that appear across many interviews signal broad patterns, not just individual opinions.
**Negative sentiment on specific themes:** This is where your product has friction or unmet expectations.
**Unexpected language:** Pay attention to the words customers use. They often reveal how to write your copy, name features, or position your product.
**Emotional signals:** Frustration, enthusiasm, and hesitation show up in how customers talk, not just what they say. Reals are especially useful for capturing this.

blocks.x: Common mistakes

items: **Stopping at 5 - 10 interviews.** Small samples create false confidence. Themes shift as more voices are added.
**Reading transcripts instead of themes.** Start with Thematic Analysis for the big picture, then drill into specific transcripts to add texture.
**Ignoring the AI Analytics Chat.** This is your fastest path from raw data to actionable insight. Ask it direct questions like "What's the top reason users mention churning?"

blocks.x: How to take action

items: Save high-signal quotes to your Notes for use in roadmap discussions or stakeholder decks.
Share Reals with your team to build shared understanding quickly.
Use recurring interview projects (e.g., monthly churn interviews) to track how sentiment shifts over time.

items.q: I'm not very technical. Can I still set this up?

a.x: Absolutely — no technical skills needed at all. The whole setup is designed to be simple and intuitive. If you can send an email, you can launch your first AI interview. Most people are up and running in under 10 minutes.

items.q: How long will it take to set up my first interview?

a.x: Just 5–10 minutes from start to finish. The AI Research Agent walks you through everything and even suggests your interview topics automatically, so you don't have to figure it all out on your own.

items.q: Can I run more than one interview project at a time?

a.x: Yes, you can! Run as many projects as you need simultaneously — one for churn research, another for concept testing, a third for post-release feedback. Each project stays neatly separate.

items.q: Do I need to start a new project every time I run a research campaign?

a.x: Not necessarily. If you're exploring the same topic with the same goals, you can keep using the same project. If your research question shifts (say, from churn to feature discovery), it's a good idea to create a new project so your data stays clean and easy to compare.

items.q: Can I see what the interview looks like before sending it to customers?

a.x: Yes — and we really encourage it! Just click your interview link and go through it as if you were a customer. You'll see exactly what they'll experience, and you can make any adjustments before sharing it widely.

items.q: How long should my interview be?

a.x: 10–15 minutes tends to be the sweet spot for most research goals. Shorter (5 minutes) is great for quick pulse checks or exit surveys. Longer (20–30 minutes) works well for deep discovery — just keep in mind that completion rates are a little lower for longer sessions.

items.q: Can I change the interview settings after it's been launched?

a.x: Once an interview is live, the settings are locked to keep your data consistent across all responses. If you need to make changes, just stop the current project and create a new one with the updated settings. It only takes a few minutes.

items.q: What languages can the AI Interviewer handle?

a.x: It supports 30+ languages. Customers can respond in whatever language feels natural to them, and you'll receive translated transcripts in your preferred language automatically.

items.q: Can I share the same link across different channels?

a.x: Yes — one link works everywhere. Email, in-app tooltips, social media, Slack, cancellation flows — wherever your customers are, the link will work.

items.q: How many people can use the same link?

a.x: As many as your plan allows. Everyone who clicks the link completes their own individual interview, so there's no limit to how many responses you can collect.

items.q: Does the interview link expire?

a.x: No — the link stays active until you decide to stop it. You're always in control of when new participants can join, and you can pause at any time while letting ongoing interviews finish.

items.q: Can I restrict who has access to the interview?

a.x: Right now, anyone with the link can access the interview. For targeted research, we recommend sharing the link only with your intended audience rather than posting it publicly — that way, you get the feedback from the right people.

items.q: What's the best way to invite customers to participate?

a.x: Context is everything. Reaching out at the right moment; right after someone cancels, just after onboarding, or immediately after using a new feature; can get you 3 to 5 times more responses than a generic feedback email. Here are a few examples that work well:

items: In a cancellation flow: "Mind sharing why you're leaving?"
After a new feature: "Just tried the new dashboard? Let us know what you think"
After onboarding: "How was your setup experience?"

items.q: Do I need to offer an incentive?

a.x: Not at all — it's completely optional. Many customers are happy to share their thoughts, especially when the interview is short, feels relevant, and they can see it might actually improve the product they use.

items.q: What kinds of incentives can I offer?

a.x: You can send Amazon gift cards directly through the platform, or you can promise discounts, free months, early feature access, or entry into a prize draw. Just make sure to follow through on whatever you offer — it goes a long way.

items.q: How much of an incentive is reasonable?

a.x: $5–$10 Amazon gift cards work nicely for 10–15 minute interviews. For longer sessions (30 minutes) or harder-to-reach audiences, $15–$25 is a good range. The key is matching the reward to the time you're asking for.

items.q: Is my interview data safe?

a.x: Yes — completely. The AI Interviewer is SOC 2 certified and GDPR compliant. All data is encrypted in transit and at rest, meeting enterprise-grade security standards.

items.q: Who can see the interview responses?

a.x: Only people with access to your Prelaunch.com account can view the data. Participants can't see each other's responses.

items.q: Can participants stay anonymous?

a.x: Yes. The interview doesn't ask for identifying information unless you specifically include a question for it. You can run fully anonymous research if that works better for your audience.

items.q: How long is my interview data stored?

a.x: Data retention depends on your account plan. Check your plan details or reach out to support@prelaunch.com and the team will be happy to clarify.

items.q: How quickly will I see results?

a.x: **Immediately.** As soon as a participant finishes their interview, the transcript, analysis, and themes show up in your dashboard. No waiting, no batch processing.

items.q: How many interviews do I need before the data means something?

a.x: Here's a helpful way to think about it:

items: 5–10 interviews: Early directional signals
20–30 interviews: Patterns start becoming meaningful
50+ interviews: You can trust the trends
100+ interviews: High confidence, reliable data

a.x: We recommend running at least 20 before drawing conclusions.

items.q: What if all my interviews say completely different things?

a.x: That's actually useful! It might mean your audience is more diverse than you expected, or that your product serves several different use cases. It could also be a signal to segment your analysis by user type — or simply that you need a few more responses before patterns emerge. Aim for 20+ before looking for consensus.

items.q: Can I export my interview data?

a.x: Yes. You can export transcripts, saved quotes from your Notes, and analysis results. Check the export options in your dashboard.

items.q: What's the difference between themes and individual quotes?

a.x: Themes show you the big picture — patterns that appear across many interviews (e.g., "pricing concerns" mentioned by 40% of participants). Individual quotes are the specific words customers used that bring those themes to life. Start with themes to understand what's happening, then use quotes to add colour and context.

items.q: It says "No interviews collected yet" — is something wrong?

a.x: Nothing's wrong at all! This just means your interview is live and ready, but no one has completed it yet. We recommend testing it yourself first, then sharing the link with your audience. Responses usually start coming in within a few hours for engaged users.

items.q: My completion rate is lower than I hoped. What can I do?

a.x: A few common reasons: the link was shared without much context, the interview felt too long, or the invitation was too generic. Try sharing the link at a natural moment of action (right after onboarding, a cancellation, or a feature use), shortening the interview if possible, making your invitation more personal, or adding a small incentive.

items.q: Can I edit an interview after it's been launched?

a.x: Not once it's live — settings are locked to keep responses consistent. But it's easy to start fresh: click "Stop Interviews," create a new project with your updated settings, and share the new link. It only takes a few minutes.

items.q: The AI Analytics Chat says it can't answer my question. Why?

a.x: A few possible reasons: there may not be enough completed interviews yet (try to have at least 5–10 before asking), the question might be too broad, or it covers a topic your interview didn't explore. Try rephrasing your question or waiting for a few more responses to come in.

items.q: What if a participant runs into a technical issue?

a.x: Just include your support email ([support@hifrank.ai](mailto:support@hifrank.ai)) in your interview invitation. The Prelaunch team can help troubleshoot or restart any failed interviews.

website-widget-embedding-frank-on-your-s.title: Website widget: embedding Frank on your site
website-widget-embedding-frank-on-your-s.lead: The Frank website widget lets researchers embed an AI interview directly into their own digital experience, instead of sending participants to a separate Frank-hosted link.

blocks.x: Why this is needed

Normally, researchers share interviews using a Frank-hosted link. Participants have to open a separate page, enter their details, go through pre-join steps, and then enter the interview room. This can feel disconnected from the site where the participant started, and may create unnecessary drop-off.
With the widget, feedback is collected directly within the researcher's own website or app — making the interview feel more natural and reducing friction for participants.
How it works for researchers
Once a research project is ready to be shared, an Embed option becomes available alongside the regular AI interviewer link. From the installation screen, researchers can:

items: Choose how the widget appears on their website (currently only the Floating widget type is available)
Customize its appearance to match their brand
Decide how participants are identified
Configure the introductory content and consent options
Select where the widget appears on the page
Preview the participant experience
Copy the installation code and add it to their website

set-up-the-frank-webhook.title: Set up the Frank webhook
set-up-the-frank-webhook.lead: When an interview is completed, Frank sends a POST to a URL you own. Use it to mark a participant as interviewed, advance them through a flow, or sync the result into your CRM or analytics — without asking Frank repeatedly whether anything has finished.

blocks.x: You configure one endpoint for the whole account. It covers every research you run; there is no per-research or per-product configuration, and no list of endpoints.

items.x: In Frank, go to **Settings → Webhooks.** Before setup the card reads **Not configured — Add an endpoint to start receiving events.**
Enter the URL that should receive events and choose **Configure webhook.**
Store the **signing secret** Frank generates. You need it to verify every incoming request, and it cannot be read back later.

blocks.alt: Webhooks settings card before setup, with the endpoint URL field
blocks.cap: Before setup: enter your URL and choose **Configure webhook.**

blocks.x: Only **public HTTPS** endpoints are accepted.

Once configured the card reads **Configured — Delivering interview events to your endpoint** and gains **Send test event**, **Rotate secret**, **Save changes** and **Delete webhook**. To change the URL later, edit the field and choose **Save changes**. Deleting stops delivery and returns the card to Not configured; you can connect a new URL afterwards.

blocks.alt: Configured Webhooks card with a masked signing secret
blocks.cap: Once configured: the secret is masked, and **Send test event** and **Rotate secret** become available.

blocks.x: **The secret cannot be viewed again.** Once the webhook exists, the **Signing secret** field shows only a masked value (`frank_whsec_••••`) — Frank will not reveal the existing secret. If you did not store it, or you need to replace it, use **Rotate secret** to generate a new value, then update your receiver to match.

sections.title: Verify the request came from Frank

blocks.x: Every request carries your secret — a `frank_whsec_`-prefixed value — in the `X-Frank-Signature` header. Verify it against your stored copy before trusting the body, and reject any request that does not match.
Frank computes:
The receiver must:

items.x: Use the **entire signing secret**, including `frank_whsec_`, exactly as shown when configuring or rotating the webhook. Do not Base64-decode it or use an API key.
Read the **original request body bytes** before JSON parsing. Parsing and reserializing JSON can change the signature.
Compare against the full header: `v1=` followed by **64 hexadecimal characters**. There is no timestamp prepended to the body.
After verification, parse the JSON and deduplicate processing using its `eventId`.

  -d '{ "persona": "olivia", "language": "en", "duration": 15 }'
Returns the research object with `status` set to active.
List researches
**GET** `/v1/researches`
Returns an array of the research object above, newest first. No parameters.

A research keeps a list of known participants. Give one private context and, when they later join an interview with the matching email, the interviewer receives that context and asks sharper questions. The context is never shown to the participant.
Add or update a participant
**PUT** `/v1/researches/{researchId}/participants`
Upserts a single participant by email. Sending the same email again updates that entry rather than creating a duplicate.
**Request body**

head: Field
Type
Notes
rows: Private interviewer notes, plain text, up to 1,000 characters. Required when adding a participant; on an update you may omit it to keep the stored value. It can never be blanked — remove the participant instead. Over 1,000 characters returns `400` and stores nothing.

Removes the participant and their private context. Past interviews they already completed are left untouched. Returns `204` with no body; an email that isn't on the list returns `404`.

Every research has three widget formats — `floating`, `inline` and `popup` — each with its own embed ID and settings. The protected domains and the widget's on/off switch are changed in the dashboard only.
List widget formats

The three formats with their embed IDs, plus the research's protected domains and whether the widget is switched on.

curl https://api.hifrank.ai/v1/researches/6b2f8c10-.../embeds \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer frank_sk_live_..."
**Response**

head: Field
Type
Notes
rows: The sites the widget may run on.
Whether the widget is switched on.

blocks.x: Get a widget format
**GET** `/v1/researches/{researchId}/embeds/{type}`
One format's settings, its install snippet — exactly what the Code tab shows — how to install it, and whether it will run. `type` is `floating`, `inline` or `popup`.
**Request**

curl https://api.hifrank.ai/v1/researches/6b2f8c10-.../embeds/floating \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer frank_sk_live_..."
**Response**

head: Field
Type
Notes
rows: This format's key; it only works with this format's snippet.
Intro copy, button labels, launcher position (floating only), identity mode and fields, consent options and appearance.
Where the snippet goes, what the page needs, what single-page apps must do, the identity placeholders to replace, and a link to the setup guide.
Whether participants can take an interview once it's installed.

What stops them: `research_draft`, `research_stopped`, `embed_revoked`, `widget_off`, `no_protected_domain`, `out_of_credits`. `out_of_credits` leaves the widget visible but stops interviews from starting; the others keep it hidden.

Every error uses the same envelope. `field` is present on validation errors and names the offending property. Every response carries an `x-request-id` header — include it when reporting an issue.

head: Status
Code
When
rows: Malformed id, or the body failed validation
Not yours, or does not exist
Product name taken, or research already has a product

blocks.x: Requests are rate limited per key. On `429` the `Retry-After` header tells you how many seconds to wait. Anything that isn't yours returns `404` rather than `403`, so ids can't be probed.
